title: Private key-value heads versus shared ones
why: It shows the layout the prose describes in sequence: in MHA each query head reads its own key and value head, so the cache scales with H; in MQA every query head reads one shared pair, so it scales with 1.
nodes: MHA: each of H query heads has its own key head and value head
MQA: all H query heads read from one shared key head and one shared value head
KV cache per token per layer: 16,384 bytes for MHA, 512 bytes for MQA
Attention arithmetic intensity: 1 FLOP/byte for MHA, 32 FLOP/byte for MQA
Ridge point = peak FLOPs / memory bandwidth; both intensities remain below it
notes: Left side: MHA layout with H private key/value subspaces feeding H query heads. Right side: MQA layout with H query heads all reading the same key/value subspace. Label cache bytes per token per layer on the KV blocks and arithmetic intensity beside each configuration. Mark the ridge point qualitatively above both intensities, since the chapter gives no numeric ridge value. No axes needed; the figure is a memory-layout comparison with labelled quantities from the prose. | Bar chart with attention variant on the x-axis and cache size per token across 32 layers on the y-axis. Label MHA at 512 KiB/token, GQA at 128 KiB/token, and MLA at 160 KiB/token, all from the chapter. Annotate the 4,096-token totals: MHA 2 GiB, GQA 512 MiB, MLA 640 MiB. Add a note that MLA is 3.2x smaller than MHA. Do not plot MQA numerically because the chapter gives no cache value for it; it appears only as the G=1 endpoint of the GQA dial. | Flow: q is multiplied by W_UKᵀ at load time to form the absorbed query; at decode the kernel multiplies that against the cached latent c and concatenates the separate per-head rotary key before scoring. On the output side, the weighted sum over latents is multiplied by W_UV, which folds into the output projection. The cache stores the latent plus the small rotary key, not full per-head key and value matrices. No numeric dimensions are labelled because the chapter gives none; only the structural quantities q, c, W_UK, W_UV, and the rotary key appear.
note: The cache scales with g, the number of KV heads, not with h, the number of query heads. Fewer KV heads means a lower arithmetic intensity, so the decode step is more bandwidth-bound.
